thread:
maria: Quick summary from today's P95-driven batcher run for route-tier gating. Ran adaptive token allocator v2 on canaries for 3h. Observations below, attaching profiler snippets and a short rollback plan.

yoav: Thanks — do you have the p95 numbers vs baseline?

maria: Baseline p95 = 240ms for chat-prod; canary with dynamic budgets = 190ms (good). But chat-lite p95 regressed from 120ms -> 220ms during peak.

shiraz: Oof. Any KV-cache delta?

maria: Yes — KV hitrate on chat-lite dropped ~18% when dynamic budgets bumped microbatch sizes for high-priority routes. Seems we evicted prefixes more aggressively.

kevin: Did the kernel selector swap during that window? i.e., long-seq kernels -> generic path?

maria: Kernel profiler shows two things: 1) frequent kernel-switch churn when sequence length distribution oscillated; 2) attention kernel inner loop had a hot path increase (likely due to misaligned SIMD for the quantized path). Pasted snippet: 

```
# perf top excerpt (canary window)
  23.4% attention_q8_kernel
  12.1% kv_cache_manager::evict
  10.6% batch_assembler::assemble_batches
  7.9% cpu_malloc
```

yoav: So effect chain: dynamic budgets -> larger microbatches for some routes -> KV churn -> lower hitrate -> more work per request -> p95 up.

maria: Exactly. Also noticed queue policy weighting favored throughput for gold-tier routes which starved chat-lite of the small-batch path.

shiraz: How did the token allocator decide per-route targets? Was it purely p95 feedback loop or combined with batch size heuristics?

maria: v2 uses a PID-style controller on p95 with a smoothing window and then translates budget to microbatch token cap via a heuristic table (route_tier -> target_tokens). But the translation doesn't account for KV residency, so it overshot for routes with heavy prefix overlap.

kevin: Can we add a quick guard: when kv_hitrate drops below threshold, clamp target_tokens down for that route?

maria: Proposed mitigation in order of ops: 
1) emergency clamp: if kv_hitrate < 70% for a route, reduce target_tokens by 30% (fast deploy).
2) change queue policy: add a "small-batch affinity" weight for routes with high prefix reuse.
3) update allocator translation: include kv_hit_factor multiplier in target computation.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: staging -> canary (adaptive-allocator v2.1, clamp rule). Requested by maria.

yoav: For a longer-term fix, we should make kernel selector aware of microbatch shape so it can pick quantized path that avoids SIMD misalignment. Also consider prefetching KV for expected prefixes when we detect rising batch sizes.

maria: Agreed. I ran a microbenchmark: when batch_size jumps from 4 -> 12, average kv_lookup latency increased 2.6x due to cache line churn. Prefetch helped median but not p95 in worst case.

shiraz: Any perf regression traces we can link?

maria: Pasted a short trace map (simplified): 
```
[request enter] -> router -> batcher::enqueue -> assemble_batches (microbatch size 12) -> kv_cache::lookup (misses) -> attention_q8_kernel (inefficient path) -> emit
```

kevin: For the emergency canary, what's the expected impact on latency and throughput?

maria: Simulation says: clamp reduces chat-lite p95 from 220ms -> 130ms, total throughput loss ~4% on the node (because microbatches shrink). Chat-prod p95 stays ~195-200ms.

yoav: Sounds acceptable. We should also add a short-running metric dashboard: per-route kv_hit, microbatch_size, p95, kernel_path_ratio.

maria: I'll add those now. Also request ops: keep canary on 2 nodes for 6h, watch kv_hit and p95. If chat-prod p95 < 200ms and chat-lite p95 < 150ms after clamp, promote.

shiraz: One more idea: change token-to-batch translation to prefer smaller batches on routes with >40% prefix overlap. That preserves KV locality.

maria: Good call. I'll update the heuristic table. Plan: deploy v2.1 clamp immediately, follow up with v2.2 (kv-aware translation) in 48h, and schedule kernel selector task to investigate q8 alignment in next sprint.

kevin: 👍 Also file a short postmortem if we hit customer-facing errors. This could've impacted low-tier customers.

maria: Will do. Adding an issue: infra/2748 "kv-churn-induced p95 regression during adaptive-batcher rollout" with links to traces and perf outputs.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: adaptive-allocator v2.1 -> node-set canary-42, canary-43.

yoav: Monitoring now. ping me if any alert fires.

maria: Thanks folks — updates in this thread as we observe metrics. :seedling:
